samples.title: The regulation cuts: each at its four steps, on the figure and the doll
samples.about: Your ask of 2026-11-06: "this haircut is not military acceptable, we should have to groom our hair the same way we will have to groom our beards and a soldier with half balding hair would 100% go fully shaved head for service." v0.0.4's horseshoe is gone: the cuts are CAREER §2's seven, men high and tight, low regulation, medium regulation or a shaved head (every thinning man's), women a regulation bun, short, or a braid pinned up. Hair grows 0.40 mm a day on every head, lived or skipped, and each cut is drawn at four steps by its sols since the barber over its due (men 10 sols, women's short 21, bun and braid 42): 0 fresh, 1 growing out (from 0.3), 2 due (from 0.7: the DI says "Haircut's due Thursday."), 3 out of regulation (from 1.0). A man's sides go from skin to a shadow, a dark and the hair's colour, his top a pixel taller at 3; a woman's short cut grows a row at the locks a step; a bun or a braid works stray pixels loose at 3. The game draws them as built until you score them. Each picture is the game's own pixels at 16 px/m (the doll at its own scale), steps left to right, each step facing you, side on and from behind.

samples.title: The rifles' drawings: the standard issue and the variety, on the weapon card and the figure
samples.about: Your lore of 2026-11-08: the Corps trains on the ground with atmospheric firearms not far from the 2020s' (it trains to fight the UN on Earth), so "Martian standard issue would look more like" your first reference, "but we would have varyiety in the guns marines carry like" your second. Five drawings, each a group: G0 the R-7 as the game draws it now, G1 and G2 the standard issue (in the reference's flat dark earth, and in the Corps' black: your decision of 2026-11-08, the Corps red and black, armour black), V1 the variety carbine, M1 the standard issue's squad marksman's rifle, a look for the R-7M. Each is drawn by the game's code (src/art/rifles.js), not painted: view a is the weapon card at its size (180 × 148) in three beliefs, on the line (28 known, chambered, on semi), at 300 m (the scope at 4×, its turrets, the dope and a hold, about 12 believed tracer) and a stovepipe looked at with a magazine of 5 tracer in the hand; view b is the chibi at 16 px/m prone, kneeling, standing aimed, at the low ready and slung, facing right, left, down and up on the bay's floor and right and left on the regolith, with the rifle alone at 16 px/m, four times larger, and at 24 px/m, and the doll holding it. View b's figures are snapped to the Mars palette as the stage snaps them (before its light and grade, which aren't applied); the card and the doll are page pictures, raw as in the game. No gun's data changes: the R-7 stays the R-7, and whichever drawing you pick becomes its drawing on the card, the figures and the doll. Star and score, then Copy my picks.

groups.title: G0: the R-7 as the game draws it (v0.0.10, for comparison)
groups.about: The game's R-7 today, unchanged: black polymer furniture and steel, the SO-4 scope, the HAD-30 with its window, the vented handguard; on the figure, tradecraft's 16-pixel rifle with the scope on top. Every other group is drawn against this one.

groups.title: G1: standard issue, after the first reference (flat dark earth)
groups.about: The first reference redrawn as the R-7: flat dark earth receivers and a slim handguard with slanted slots and a rail along its top, the low-power scope on a cantilever mount (its throw lever, the offset dot at its front), the angled foregrip, a light on the rail's front, the short ported brake, the black side-folding skeleton stock, a flared well, the black polymer magazine, bulkier than the grip, ribbed low. The tan is the Mars palette's butterscotch dust, its light, base and dark one step apart, so the stage keeps them. On the figure: the black stock to the receiver, the body tan and lit along its top to the brake, the scope dark with a glint of glass at its front, the grip and the foregrip tan, the magazine in gun metal so it shows against the outline.

groups.title: G2: standard issue in the Corps' black
groups.about: G1's rifle all black, for your decision of 2026-11-08 (the factions' colours: the MCRN and the Corps red and black, armour black, ceremonial red and black): black receivers and handguard over the black polymer stock, scope and magazine. Black is drawn as the steel greys' lowest steps, so the parts stay apart: the receivers and the handguard a step lighter than the stock and the scope, lit along the top, the slots the darkest, the brake and the light on the rail as on G1. On the figure the stage's snap puts the body's base and the gun metal of the stock and the scope on one colour, the steel greys' 0.38 step, so the rifle is one black, a step clear of the ink outline so the outline doesn't swallow it, with its top lit a step lighter from the receiver to the brake to give its line against the utilities and the floor. No red on it (my call): the Corps' red is ceremonial and this is field kit, black like the armour; and red already means something on the card (the selector's fire mark, the SEMI and TR words, the tracer noses) and, on a 16 px/m figure, a red pixel reads as a tracer or a wound, so a red band or badge would read as a signal or as decoration, not as the Corps'. Everything else as G1.

groups.title: V1: variety carbine, after the second reference (sand, clear magazine)
groups.about: A different carbine a marine may carry, a step lighter than the standard issue so the two read apart by value as well as shape: one sand polymer body (the receiver and the handguard together, rounded at its front, thin vents), the carry handle with a rail on it and a boxed holographic sight on the rail, the skeleton folding stock with its web, a short rail on the handguard's side, the black vertical grip, a pronged flash hider, and the clear smoked magazine with the believed rounds seen through it, staggered, each with its nose (red when believed tracer). On the figure: the sight dark with its glint on the handle's hump, the handle's opening under it, the stock's hole, the vertical grip, the smoked magazine.

groups.title: M1: the squad marksman's rifle, a look for the R-7M (my design)
groups.about: The standard issue's family stretched to the R-7M's row in WEAPONS §3.2 (101 cm, a heavy free-floated barrel, the HAD-30, a 3 to 12× scope with a rangefinder, a bipod; no suppressor, which is the S-9's): flat dark earth receivers, a fixed precision stock (an adjustable cheek riser, a butt with spacers, a monopod's knob), a longer slotted handguard with the bipod folded forward under it (hinge block, legs, feet), the heavy barrel and a ported brake, the bigger scope with its rangefinder's box. The R-7M is not the R-7: it would be its drawing only if you want the marksman's rifle to have one; no data changes.

samples.title: The hit card: a turner hit, drawn as a range target is (A the doll, B the khaki board, C the casualty card)
samples.about: Your words of 2026-11-07: "Targets in game should be represented with the same logic we represent the shooting range targets, drawn with impact points drawn as well, using similar to inventory and character menu drawings of people." One string's marks on a turner at 7 m: a Pair to the chest, a third round high, a fourth missed. Left, what the marine could tell during the string (belief): a hollow ring where his sight was at each break, filled when he saw it strike, numbered. Right, the debrief (truth): the holes where they went, coloured by zone (A red, C orange, the head crimson), the calls faint under them, the coach's line. A is the doll of PERSONNEL and the inventory in colour, the man-target's zones over it at 25% (the game draws A until you score them); B the khaki man-target board, the outline and kit in its two tones, holes in ink; C the casualty card's front and back outlines. Each in the hit card's box at 1024 × 768 (--ui 0.85: the card drawn at 170 px, its whole pixels), 1600 × 900 (--ui 1.25) and 1920 × 1080 (--ui 1.5), at whole pixels where they fit. Star the look you want; the card goes where it shows, at the top left under the toasts on Bang.

samples.title: The look: five scenes with their people, in the four candidates
samples.about: The first look round put together: the kit's scenes (samples/scenes) with the real figures in them (samples/figures, one instanced draw), lit by the scene's mood, in the game's own frame (zoom 1, 40 × 22.5 m), or zoomed twice where a splash would frame it (L2, L5). Each scene is shown four ways, the two open questions crossed: the density (16 px/m at 640 × 360, tradecraft's; or 24 px/m at 960 × 540) by row, and the figures (A, chibi, about 2.4 heads, tradecraft's; or B, soldier, about 3.8 heads) by column. Nothing else changes inside a scene's four pictures: the same people in the same places at the same moment. Shots are the picture's own pixels at × 2, so both densities fill the same width here; click one to see it larger and flip between the four with the arrow keys. Star what you like and give each a score out of 100, then Copy my picks and paste it back.

groups.title: The squad bay at reveille
groups.about: Echo Company's east wing at Base Melas (PLACES §4.4): three squad bays, the hallway, the heads and the lounge, the overheads on before the sky is light. Thirteen marines get up: you in PT kit down the 1st squad's aisle, one dressing at an open wall locker, one on a footlocker lacing his shoes, one in a towel heading out for the head, the squad leader (a sergeant in utilities) calling the 2nd squad, a late riser still asleep on an upper rack, one making her rack, two of the 3rd squad out to formation, one at the study table, the fire watch by his desk in the hallway, one at head A's basins. Zoom 1: the game's frame, 40 × 22.5 m.

groups.title: The valley floor: two marines in vac suits, by day and in a dust storm
groups.about: Melas Chasma's floor by the Talus 3 station (the vehicle lock, the dust vestibule, a scarp of layered deposits). A suit drill: you in the light vac suit, rifle at the low ready, walking back up to the vehicle lock; the other in the low-g bound at 0.38 g (the lope's apex, 0.45 m up, the shadow under it shrunk), rifle slung. a to d by a clear day; e to h in a dust storm of optical depth 4 (VIEWS §2.7: the sun at a tenth, sight about 100 m, dust falling and blowing), the fog of awareness round you (what you aren't looking at veiled), the other marine a shape in the haze at the edge of your sight. Zoom 1.

groups.title: A frigate's deck 5 at battle stations: strapped into a crash couch
groups.about: A Hellas-class frigate's marine deck under battle red (the panels at a third, the red strips; the ship palette). You lie strapped into a crash couch in the ready room, helmet sealed; a marine two couches along with his helmet off and clipped to his pack, another in the row behind; one sits on the one couch whose harness is still open, about to strap in; the section's NCO in the aisle, helmet off. Lying in this projection: a body on its back, head north, is seen from its feet, so it looks much like a figure standing (VIEWS §3.5); the couch round it and the long shadow say it lies. Zoom 2 (20 × 11.25 m) on the ready room, as a splash would frame it; the whole deck is 17.4 × 15.4 m.
